claim: FLS2 is a typical receptor kinase in Arabidopsis thaliana that recognizes the conserved 22 amino acid sequence in the N-terminal region of flagellin (flg22) to initiate plant defense pathways.
source: The Arabidopsis thaliana FLAGELLIN-SENSITIVE2 (FLS2), a typical receptor kinase, recognizes the conserved 22 amino acid sequence in the N-terminal region of flagellin (flg22) to initiate plant defense pathways, which was intensively studied in the past decades.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established background information about FLS2 function.

claim: The phosphorylation of Ser-938 in FLS2 impacts its spatiotemporal dynamics and lifetime upon flg22 treatment.
source: Through single-particle tracking, we demonstrated that upon flg22 treatment the phosphorylation of Ser-938 in FLS2 impacts its spatiotemporal dynamics and lifetime.
evidence: The abstract states this was demonstrated through single-particle tracking experiments.

claim: Flg22 treatment increased the co-localization of GFP-tagged FLS2 with AtRem1.3-mCherry.
source: Following Förster resonance energy transfer-fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy and protein proximity indexes assays revealed that flg22 treatment increased the co-localization of GFP-tagged FLS2/FLS2S938D but not FLS2S938A with AtRem1.3-mCherry, a sterol-rich lipid marker, indicating that the phosphorylation of FLS2S938 affects FLS2 sorting efficiency to AtRem1.3-associated nanodomains.
evidence: The abstract describes results from FRET-FLIM and protein proximity index assays showing increased co-localization.
